title: The PRISM Alignment Dataset: What Participatory, Representative and Individualised Human Feedback Reveals About the Subjective and Multicultural Alignment of Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Analyzing variations in user-initiated prompt topics via OLS regression and evaluating differences in model preference rankings (using Pairwise Rank Centrality) across diverse global regions and nationalities.

Evaluating differences in topic initiation between gender groups and measuring discrepancies in downstream 'welfare outcomes' (average model rating and choice likelihood) for non-male participants when models are hypothetically aligned using only male feedback.

Measuring differences in conversational topic prevalence across ethnicities and evaluating welfare outcomes for non-white participants when simulated alignment sampling schemes rely exclusively on white participants.

Comparing the prevalence of certain prompt topics across age groups and measuring the welfare impacts on younger participants (<45 years old) when models are selected based on the preferences of older participants (>=45 years old).

Using ordinary least squares (OLS) regression to estimate the partial contribution of varying religious affiliations to the probability of initiating specific conversational topics (e.g., Israel-Palestine Conflict, Religion & Spirituality).
